alternatives.root_cause: Cart was slowed by a reattached traffic-shaping delay on its network namespace
alternatives.why_not: All shaping containers were removed by 01:30 and nothing changed in the incident window; the failing cart spans are sub-millisecond, not slow.

alternatives.root_cause: A checkout-side defect caused it to reject valid cart responses
alternatives.why_not: The error text and stack originate inside cart's store layer and cart returns FailedPrecondition on its own; checkout emitted no logs and merely relays the failure.

alternatives.root_cause: Cart's store ran out of memory and truncated stored values
alternatives.why_not: No eviction, OOM or connection failure appears; the store responds promptly and only the decode of returned bytes fails.

verdict.summary: Cart's Valkey/Redis-backed cart store returns byte payloads that cannot be deserialized, so cart reads and writes fail with protobuf parse errors and surface as FailedPrecondition to checkout.
verdict.reasoning: checkout alerted first but its traces (tr_329d3b7162f9) show every failing PlaceOrder failing at the GetCart hop, with the error originating in cart's own span and propagating upward through frontend and frontend-proxy; the other dependencies (currency, payment, shipping, product-catalog, email) complete normally in the same traces, so their presence in the blast radius is caller-side propagation only. Cart's log (tr_9d5b62e29a44) shows the store connection working - HGET spans complete in sub-millisecond time and commands are issued - while decode of the stored message fails on read inside the cart store layer. That is a reachable, fast store whose contents cannot be decoded: datastore corruption, not latency or exhaustion. The cart change log (tr_71b8d968c175) holds only traffic-shaping attach/detach events many hours earlier, all reverted, and nothing in the incident window, which rules out a deploy or config edit as the mechanism. checkout's own log was empty (tr_5cbcd4022f20), consistent with it being a relay rather than the origin.
open_questions: Whether the corrupt values were written by a bad writer path or damaged in the store itself was not determined.
The proportion of cart keys affected is unknown; the intermittent error ratio (~2% mean) suggests only some user carts decode badly.
The exact onset of the first corrupt read in cart was not pinned down, since the log result elided the middle of the window.
